title: Aminist 21 validation: fixed baseline recipes
optimizer: SGD; no learning-rate schedule; no Nesterov
configuration_policy: Only recipe, seed, and device may be selected. Every dataset uses identical recipe hyperparameters, selected before scoring. No warm starts, checkpoints, early stopping, or query-label access.
rng: CPU torch initialization; NumPy PCG64 shuffling. Independent PCG64([member_seed,20260922]) affine schedule. Ensemble member seeds seed+11*i.

initialization.linear_mlp_cnn: Construct all CPU layers, then Kaiming-uniform fan_in ReLU weight reset and zero biases.
initialization.reversible: Four 41x41 branch matrices drawn independently Normal(0,0.05/sqrt(41)); ordinary torch Linear(82,10) constructor initialization for classifier.

architecture_notes.mlp: Biased Linear/ReLU hidden layers and biased 10-class output.
architecture_notes.cnn: 3x3, stride1, padding1, bias-free convolution and ReLU at every stage; no pooling, dropout or batchnorm. Flatten all spatial coordinates; biased head/ReLU/output.
architecture_notes.reversible: Zero-pad normalized81-pixel vector to82, split41/41. Each block performs two additive couplings with ReLU-before-linear. Custom backward reconstructs states and saves one endpoint plus weights. Classifier is not reversible.

interpretation: These fixed references establish empirical ranges, not universal acceptable accuracy thresholds. The cnn32-ensemble3 recipe is inspired by the earlier 97% MNIST procedure but uses native PyTorch cross-entropy, native interpolation and independently specified shuffling; it is not a bitwise port of the ordered-arithmetic submission. The reversible reference uses the earlier architecture and 2-epoch SGD settings but a portable eager runner.
reproducibility: Bitwise equality expected only for repeated execution in the same pinned software/hardware environment; cross-CPU/GPU equality is not promised. All returned model, schedule, logit and prediction hashes are recorded.
